haiku-low.q1: Its search document is deleted. A c or u event with after.status not active triggers a versioned delete by id, since only active rows may appear in search.
haiku-low.q2: The older change is refused as a version conflict. It is counted as stale and acked, not treated as an error, so the newer data stays.
haiku-low.q3: It retries with backoff of 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, capped at 60 s. The partition pauses, its offset does not move, and it never skips ahead.
haiku-low.q4: The event, error, partition and offset go to the DLQ topic catalog.products.dlq. The event is acked, an alert fires, and processing continues.
haiku-low.q5: At 20 GB an alert fires. At 50 GB ops drop search_slot, live sync stops, and a full rebuild is the only way back, creating a new slot.
haiku-low.q6: An atomic alias swap moves products to products_v4 in one request. It happens only when the snapshot is done, lag is under 5 s, and the count is within 0.5 percent of active rows.
haiku-low.q7: Progress is kept as per-partition offsets for each consumer group. An offset advances only up to the last contiguous acked event, after those events are acked.
haiku-low.q8: Unacked events are replayed when it restarts. Offsets only moved up to the last contiguous acked event, and the version rule makes the replay harmless.
haiku-low.q9: A replay start offset is recorded before the snapshot opens, and group products-rebuild-v4 applies every event from there. Events below S are stale and counted.
haiku-low.q10: Every document written by the bulk copy carries version S, the WAL position read as the snapshot's first statement.
haiku-low.q11: products-live keeps writing products_v3 for 48 hours, so alias swap-back is rollback. After 48 hours, products-live stops and products_v3 is deleted. Reconcile stale hard-deleted ids first.
haiku-low.q12: Search keeps serving products_v3, since the alias moves only at the switch. A failed copy means dropping products_v4 and taking a new DBA-approved snapshot. A failed catch-up is handled by retry or re-snapshot.

sonnet.q1: The document is deleted by id, with the version. A c or u event whose after.status is not active triggers a delete. Deleting an absent document counts as success. A versioned delete cannot remove a newer write.
sonnet.q2: The write is refused as a version conflict. It is counted as stale and acked, and it is not treated as an error. The newer data stays.
sonnet.q3: It retries failed items with backoff of 1 s, 2 s, 4 s and so on, capped at 60 s. The partition is paused and its offset does not move. It never skips ahead. Lag grows, and the 5 s SLO alert fires first.
sonnet.q4: The event, the error, the partition and the offset are written to the DLQ topic catalog.products.dlq. An alert fires, the event is acked and processing continues. If the DLQ write fails, it backs off and retries only the DLQ write, and the partition stays paused until the DLQ accepts it. Replaying the DLQ after a fix is manual and not covered. The change counts as an SLO miss.
sonnet.q5: Ops drop search_slot at 50 GB retained WAL to protect the primary. The connector stops and live sync stops. A full rebuild is the only way back. The rebuild creates a new slot, then a snapshot and replay fill a new index. The alias moves to it once the gate passes. An operator starts the rebuild. An alert fires at 20 GB.
sonnet.q6: One atomic alias swap on products removes products_v3 and adds products_v4 in a single request. The gate must pass first. The snapshot must be done, lag must be under 5 s, and the products_v4 count must be within 0.5 percent of the active row count.
sonnet.q7: Progress is stored as Kafka consumer group offsets, one per partition. The offset is committed only up to the last contiguous acked event. An event counts as acked after a successful write, a stale conflict, or a DLQ write. The offset is committed after the bulk write results are in, not at poll.
sonnet.q8: Unacked events are replayed. Events that were already written are replayed too. The version rule makes the replay harmless, because equal versions are accepted and older ones are stale. No alert is raised.
sonnet.q9: The connector streams from a slot that exists before S is read. The replay start offset per partition is recorded before the snapshot opens. A separate group, products-rebuild-v4, reads the topic from those offsets with the same version, retry and DLQ rules. Commits after S land after the recorded offset. Events below S are stale and counted. Events at or above S apply on top of the snapshot.
sonnet.q10: Every snapshot document carries version S. S is the WAL LSN read as the first statement of the repeatable-read snapshot.
sonnet.q11: products-live keeps writing products_v3 for 48 hours after the switch. Rollback is swapping the alias back, and no change made after the switch is lost. After 48 hours products-live is stopped and products_v3 is deleted. Caveat: products_v3 holds cron-era state, so documents for rows hard-deleted before the switch may remain. Reconcile it against active ids first, or accept that risk.
sonnet.q12: Search is unaffected. The rebuild writes only to products_v4, never to the alias, and the alias stays on products_v3 until the gate passes. If the gate fails, it keeps consuming, alerts if it does not converge, and does not switch. If the snapshot reader crashes, the snapshot cannot resume, so products_v4 contents are dropped, the control record is reset, and a new DBA-approved snapshot is needed. If replay offsets are past the 7-day retention, it drops products_v4 and restarts from a new snapshot. Live sync into products_v3 continues. A catch-up failure that is not covered by those cases is NOT STATED.
